# NOTES ON THE TEXT (two books; compact reference)

## BOOK 1: OLGA ROMANOFF (Griffith, George Chetwynd; Gutenberg 54096; pub. 1897, illustrated by Fred T. Jane)

Frontispiece: "Evil in such a shape might be something more than good." Dedicated to Hiram Stevens Maxim.

**PROLOGUE: The Prophecy of Natas.** Written by Israel di Murska (Natas, Master of the Terror), year 1930, 25th year of Peace. Festival of Deliverance on 8 Dec (Anniversary of Victory, the 1904 battle of London). Key content: Richard Arnold (Englishman) made first self-powered flying ship, 1903; Alan Tremayne united Anglo-Saxon race; Alexander Romanoff (last Tsar) led Franco-Slavonian League, besieged London; Natasha ("Angel of the Revolution," Natas's daughter) pleaded for mercy. Russians slain; Tsar and princes exiled to Siberia. Aerians (Terrorists' descendants in mountain valley of Aeria, Central Africa) hold air command. Prophecy: in 2030 power returns to rulers; in 5th generation a fiery messenger from the stars brings doom; chosen few survive. Sign of flaming sword. Festival of Deliverance readings every fifth year.

**Ch I. The Surrender of the World-Throne.** 8 Dec 2030, St Paul's Cathedral, London. President Alan Arnold (descendant of Alan Tremayne, Richard Arnold, Natasha) surrenders world rule; keeps air empire ("we will command the air"). Speech on Natas's prophecy.

**Ch II. A Crowned King.** Same night, Hampstead turret. Paul Romanoff (~100 yrs old, dying; great-grandson of Alexander, Tsar) and granddaughter Olga Romanoff (~16-17, beautiful, imperious) and Serge Nicholaivitch (22, Prince of Romanoff; Dagmar's line). Paul takes a drug (two vials: colourless liquids turn red) to revive briefly. Oath before ikon: take his ashes to Petersburg (Church of Peter and Paul), then marry at Moscow Uspenski Sobor. Secret cavity behind oak panel holds imperial crown of Russia (stolen in Kremlin plunder). Paul recounts: Vladimir Romanoff (Olga's father) killed by Supreme Council in Norway forest for building air-ship; Paul's secret will. Paul dies while raising crown.

**Ch III. Tsarina Olga.** Paul's ashes at Highgate Crematorium; registered as "Paul Ivanitch"; Olga and Serge pose as siblings "Ivanitch." Olga crowns herself Tsarina; Serge crowned Tsar. Secret will: 400 names of descendants of ruined nobles; weapons section; power conversion of coal to electricity; explosives formulae; a hidden parchment slip. Olga seduces Serge into leaving her alone to read it; she removes the slip.

**Ch IV. A Son of the Gods.** Journey on Eastern express (Continental station, London to Pekin, 150-200 mph); Channel Bridge at Dover-Calais. Alan Arnoldson (son of President) and Alexis Masarov (Alexis Mazanoff descendant) met with Alderman Heatherstone. Olga flirts with Alan; Serge jealous. Alan explains Aerian pledge of silence; Coming Race/Vril reference; Alan claims he could kill with a glance.

**Ch V. A Vision from the Clouds.** At Königsberg express splits. Olga postpones wedding (plan in Berlin). Air-ship Ithuriel (blue-metal hull, ~200 ft, 10 guns) appears; Alan invites Olga and Serge for voyage next day from St Petersburg. Olga: "by this time to-morrow you shall be my slave."

**Ch VI. Deed and Dream.** Olga's laboratory in hotel: prepares two liquids: white narcotic (sleep) and dark blue "elixir" (will-poison, two drops). Dream vision of Aeria valley (lake, marble city, golden dome, silver winged woman statue) and of death-world. Serge's breakfast; plans to seize Ithuriel. Shows "Elixir of Death" flask on chain.

**Ch VII. The Spell of Circe.** Sleigh race (Olga wins); Peter-and-Paul fortress memorial plate to Natas. Skating; Alan's wheel-skates. Olga and Serge plan drugging crew. Supper; Olga drugs punch; Serge becomes automaton ("I am your slave"). Ithuriel arrives at hotel garden next morning, Olga boards.

**Ch VIII. The New Terror.** Ithuriel vanishes; Norway snowdrift finds eight dead Aerian crew. Olga's "New Terror": submarine warfare; transports Massilia, Ceres, Astraea vanish; Sirius wreck; 1st May 2036 a ball of metal falls in Aeria with Olga's letter (island near 40th parallel S, 120th meridian W). Sultan Khalid the Magnificent (Egypt, Alexandria; 34 years old; 700 million subjects).

**Ch IX. The Flight of the "Revenge."** Olga renamed Ithuriel the Revenge. Pursuit by Aerian ships Ariel and Ithuriel; Boris Lossenski and Levin Ostroff gunners, Olga makes them princes. Antarctic battle; Russian fleet of 31 destroyed; Olga's fury. Council meeting: fear of Romanoff.

**Ch X. Strange Tidings to Aeria.** Alan's letter: he and Alexis drugged, now freed; took submarine Narwhal; will attack Kerguelen. Council restores them command. Alma Tremayne (Alan's fiancée, ~19, grey eyes, dusky-brown hair; tall) alone on terrace; her pain. Isma Arnold (Alan's sister, golden hair, sunny-blue eyes) arrives in swan-prowed boat Cygna.

**Ch XI. The Snake in Eden.** Isma and Alma talk in Cygna over Mars rising; Isma: forgiveness; "jealousy" lesson from Mars. Alma weeps. Parents' family council; Isma pleads for Alan and Alexis.

**Ch XII. The Battle of Kerguelen.** Kerguelen (Desolation Land) station, Christmas Harbour; commanders Max Ernstein (Cachalot), Edward Forrest (Ariel, admiral). Narwhal ram attack on Russian scouts via needle detector; battle; Russian attacks repulsed by batteries and Ariel. Alan's submarine ambush sinks Russian squadron.

**Ch XIII. The Syren's Stronghold.** Alan's report: Mount Terror in Antarctica (Russian stronghold; Kishenov, Louis Khemski). Alexis plan: Narwhal blocks subterranean tunnel with twelve torpedoes. Crew led by chief engineer George Cosmo.

**Ch XIV. From the Sea to the Air.** Narwhal returns; Council reply: Alan and Alexis command Ithuriel; 100 air-ships to be built. Isma's letter and photographs to Alan; Alexis gets Isma's letter. Alexis renames captured Vindaya "Isma" later.

**Ch XV. Olga in Council.** Olga rebukes Michael Lossenski; Orloff Lossenski advises alliance with Sultan; Mount Terror damage; Olga resolves to crown herself Tsarina.

**Ch XVI. Khalid the Magnificent.** Lossenski arrives at Alexandria with Olga's letter; Ithuriel (Alan, Alexis) captures Vindaya at palace terrace; Alan kills Moslem guard with blue-flame rapier; Alan demands pledge of peace for one year; demonstrates over Crete islet.

**Ch XVII. An Unholy Alliance.** Olga's air-fleet (Revenge) at Alexandria; she charms Khalid; Grand Vizier Musa al Ghazi drugged; Mecca visit; Olga promises to convert Russia to Islam; Musa's counsel.

**Ch XVIII. A Momentous Commission.** Vindaya renamed Isma. Fleet of 50 air-ships to Alexandria with ultimatum; Olga confronts Alan on palace roof; Alan's message to Sultan.

**Ch XIX. Face to Face Again.** Olga tears ultimatum; tries to shoot Alan; Khalid intervenes; Olga accuses Alan of crimes (murdering Serge, sinking crew); Sultan deceived. Alan returns to Ithuriel; Olga's letter threatens attacks.

**Ch XX. The Call to Arms.** Alan visits King Albert II at Windsor; Alan asserts Federation rule; Parliament defiance.

**Ch XXI. The Home-Coming.** 11 May 2037; Alan and Alexis return; Council restores golden wings; Avenger (Alan's new flagship, 600 mph); Alma's heart; Isma and Alexis reunite.

**Ch XXII. The Eve of Battle.** Restoration ceremony; war preparations; Aerian fleet of 400; farewell.

**Ch XXIII. The First Blow.** 16 May 2037: Avenger destroys Alexandria air-ships; Moslem transports (5 fleets) sunk by submarines (Max Ernstein's electro-magnet and phonetic indicator technology); Khalid watches.

**Ch XXIV. War at Its Worst.** Avenger strikes Moscow scouts; Gibraltar bridge; Alexis captures Moslem "Haroun" at Russian frontier; aerial battle at Russian frontier; Aerian recall order (Alan's signature, 16 May, 6 P.M.).

**Ch XXV. A Message from Mars.** Vassilis Cosmo (astronomer; brother of George Cosmo) receives Martian photo-telegraph message: comet doom on 23 Sept 2037. Council meets; Natas's sealed document read (interpretation of 1920 comet; caverns of Mount Austral).

**Ch XXVI. Sentence of Death.** Heads of families told; Council grants Alan, Alma, Isma exemption; Alan refuses; mother's pleas; Alexis swears to go with Alan.

**Ch XXVII. Alma Speaks.** Palm grove at lake; Alma asks forgiveness; they re-betroth; "only you can bid me live, Alma."

**Ch XXVIII. The Sign in the Sky.** Caverns of Mount Austral; water-gate; Council refuses air-ship departure two months; Fire-Cloud comet appears 15 July.

**Ch XXIX. The Truce of God.** Sluice-gate tested; Alan and Alexis marry Alma and Isma (31 July). Avenger renamed Alma. Visit to Alexandria; Sultan refuses; Olga arrives in Revenge; Olga attempts to shoot Alma; Alan's rebuke. Fleet departs.

**Ch XXX. The Shadow of Death.** Olga mocks; Musa and Hakem confirm; Olga tries shooting Alma; Alan fires, cutting Olga's forehead; Lossenski killed. World's collapse; Aeria epidemic; population dwindling.

**Ch XXXI. The Last Battle.** Lake floods valley; Olga and Khalid's fleet attacks; battle at Aeria's walls; Alan, Alexis, Alma, Isma fight; doors closed 22-23 Sept.

**Ch XXXII. The She-Wolf to Her Lair.** Olga flees to Mount Terror with Khalid (shot through lung by Boris); Olga poisons crew; shoots Boris; Khalid wounded; they shelter in Mount Terror during fire-storm.

**Epilogue. "Vengeance Is Mine."** Refugees emerge late Sept; Aeria a swamp; Alan and Alma find Olga at Mount Terror; Olga insane, paralysed; Alan dead in her arms (Khalid's bullet, no, Alan dead by fire); Alma: "God forgive her."

Advertisements for Angel of the Revolution, A Heroine of the Slums, Great War in England in 1897, Captain of the Mary Rose.

---

## BOOK 2: THE ROMANCE OF GOLDEN STAR (Griffith; Gutenberg 20173; "The Romance of Golden Star"; pub. 1897 by F. V. White; illustrated by Alfred Pearse)

Frontispiece caption: "Hail, Son of the Sun!" (p. 78). Epigraph: Prophecy of Vilcaroya-Inca and Golden Star, his sister-bride: "To that Son of the Sacred Race who, for honour and faith and love, shall take the hand of a pure virgin of his own holy blood..." shall cast out the Oppressor and raise the Rainbow Banner above the Golden Throne of the Incas.

**PROLOGUE (Mummy).** London, Maida Vale house. Professor Martin Lamson (archaeologist, South American antiquities, just back from Peru/Bolivia); Dr Laurens Djama (physiologist, ~32, slender, olive skin, black hair, blue-black eyes; sister Ruth = Joyful Star). Mummy of an Inca prince, found by Lamson in valley 4 days' ride west of Cuzco, by a lake under masonry (near the Apurimac, Abancay route); lying supine, unembalmed (unique). Djama proposes revival experiment; Mephistopheles bargain (half of treasure). Djama resuscitates mummy in his laboratory in Brondesbury Park/Kilburn. Lamson faints. Inca wakes: "Am I only dreaming that the death-sleep is over?" Says "Cori-Coyllur, Nustallipa, Nusta mi!" (Golden Star, my princess). Vilcaroya-Inca, son of Huayna-Capac; year 1532 (Atahuallpa captured at Cajamarca, Huascar slain). Vilcaroya wants Golden Star restored.

**Ch I. Back Through the Shadows.** Vilcaroya's narration. Joyful Star (Ruth) named Cusi-Coyllur. Captain Francis Hartness (English soldier, ~30, blue eyes, golden hair/beard) joins them at Panama. Route: Arequipa (Misti volcano), Sicuani, Cacha, Piquillacta, Cuzco. Vilcaroya swears vengeance.

**Ch II. Brothers of the Blood.** Hacienda near Cuzco sought (2,000 pounds). Vilcaroya visits San Sebastian; Tupac-Rayca (chief, great-grandson of Tupac-Amaru) and Ullullo. Joyful Star says "I'd rather be a savage"? No: she defends the Indians; Djama sneers. Vilcaroya reveals Golden Star is his sister; Ruth horrified; Hartness explains sister-marriage impossibility. Vilcaroya accepts; loves Ruth.

**Ch III. In the Hall of Gold.** Vilcaroya follows Djama (ten dollars to Ullullo). Rodadero plain; Sayacusca (Tired Stone) cleft; underground stone door; Hall of Gold; imperial robes of Huascar; Vilcaroya crowned. Djama blindfolded; Hall of Gold seen; Tupac's homage. Gold ingots sold to buy hacienda.

**Ch IV. The Sister Stars.** Journey to valley of Golden Star's tomb; twin peaks (Umantai/Saljantai); Rio de la Banca bridge; secret rock door; Golden Star's tomb; Joyful Star resembles Golden Star. Hartness and Ruth attraction; Djama's jealousy.

**Ch V. How Djama Did His Work.** Djama revives Golden Star; "Evil Eyes" threatens; holds Vilcaroya to conditions; Vilcaroya threatens with dagger. Djama demands Golden Star; swaps: Joyful Star for Golden Star.

**Ch VI. The Waking of Golden Star.** Ruth awakens Golden Star with a kiss; Golden Star's mind a blank. Ruth's peacemaking. Vilcaroya and Hartness become brothers-in-arms; Peru in civil war; plans.

**Ch VII. In the Throne-Room of Yupanqui.** Ruth nurses Golden Star. Djama's request for reward; Hartness proposes Golden Star to England. Golden Star shrinks from Djama. Ruth shown the treasure; Vilcaroya proposes to Ruth in the throne-room of Yupanqui.

**Ch VIII. How the Soul of Golden Star Came Back.** Vilcaroya presents Ruth as his Coya; Golden Star's memory returns; Tupac's Ayllos; Hartness named war-chief. Djama and professor sworn to secrecy.

**Ch IX. The Treachery of Djama.** Djama betrays Vilcaroya to Governor Antonio Prada (his son, Coronel Prada, a Spanish officer, tricked into Hall of Gold). Djama and Spanish officer imprisoned in golden cells. Professor Lamson chooses to stay; Djama's gold madness.

**Ch X. On the Rodadero.** Ruth pleads for Djama; Golden Star and Ruth dressed as Coyas. Anahuac reports. Vilcaroya kills sentries with knife. Hartness takes command.

**Ch XI. How We Took the City of the Sun.** Trap at Sayacusca; Governor Prada surrenders; battle in the Plaza; machine-guns of Cuartel; Cuzco taken.

**Ch XII. Queen and Crown.** Ruth as Vilcaroya's queen; Hartness appointed Governor; Djama's cell; Vilcaroya crowned Inca at Sun festival.

**Ch XIII. How Djama Paid His Debt.** Djama attacks Vilcaroya with rifle; Ullullo killed; Djama suicides by will (death of Djama by will).

**Ch XIV. The Re-Kindling of the Sacred Fire.** Feast of Raymi; Golden Star and Vilcaroya; Joyful Star and Vilcaroya marry (marriage font of wine and water); Hartness and Golden Star marry. Restoration of Inca empire; book written by Hartness and professor. Footnote: Santo Domingo church on site of Temple of the Sun.

Printer's corrections: "Anahauc" corrected to "Anahuac"; "ont" to "out"; "Ullulo" to "Ullullo".
